title: In Joanna Natasegara’s Oscar Contender ‘The Disciple,’ Wu-Tang Clan Superfan Cilvaringz Morphs Into A Killer Bee
summary: Joanna Natasegara’s documentary The Disciple gains Oscar buzz, raising demand for music-centric docs and related performance opportunities.
content: Wu-Tang Clan has big plans for Thanksgiving. The hip-hop legends will be in Detroit to headline the halftime show for the NFL game between the host Lions and the Chicago Bears (U2 will do the halftime honors for the Thanksgiving Eve game in LA between the Green Bay Packers and the Los Angeles Rams, airing on Netflix ). Wu-Tang, founded in Staten Island, NY, has long been considered one of the most influential groups in music history, with legions of fans worldwide and even their own acolytes known as the Killa Bees, a collective of rappers, producers, singers and others affiliated with the group. Among the most notable Bees: Cilvaringz , aka Tarik Azzougarh , a Dutch Moroccan Wu-Tang superfan turned artist whose connection to the Clan goes back to the late 1990s. The remarkable story of how Cilvaringz became associated with Wu-Tang and then played a critical role in producing the astonishing one-copy only album Once Upon a Time in Shaolin is told in the documentary The Disciple: A Wu-Tang Fable , now streaming on Netflix. Watch on Deadline The Oscar-contending film is directed by Joanna Natasegara, the Academy Award-winning producer of The White Helmets , The Edge of Democracy , Virunga and other acclaimed documentaries. The Disciple premiered at the Sundance Film Festival in January and screened in September at the Telluride Film Festival before debuting on Netflix. DEADLINE: Have you always been into Wu-Tang? When did you learn about the story of Tarik Azzougarh? Joanna Natasegara: I grew up in the ’90s. It’s exactly my era of music… Wu-Tang was just something me and my friends were very much into. We would go to clubs and listen to hip hop music, but it was something I just didn’t really think about in the scope of my work, clearly for decades, actually. And so, the story [of Tarik/Cilvaringz] itself I hadn’t heard of despite it being something that had gone around the world. title: ‘The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping’: Creating Glenn Close’s Over-the-Top Looks by Leaning Into Drusilla’s ‘Narcissist’ Nature
summary: Glenn Close’s narcissistic Drusilla drives extravagant styling, signaling significant character-driven collaboration opportunities with costume and makeup teams.
content: Being a member of Capitol society in Panem is an honor not to be taken lightly, at least if you’re Drusilla Sickle, played by screen legend Glenn Close in “The Hunger Games : Sunrise on the Reaping.” In the book, Drusilla is the cruel and vain escort for Haymitch Abernathy (Joseph Zada) and the rest of the District 12 tributes in the 50th Hunger Games, where she uses over-the-top fashion to broadcast her social status. Close worked closely with costume designer Bina Daigeler and hair, makeup and prosthetics designer Natalie MacGowan Spencer to ensure the character translated properly from Suzanne Collins’ bestselling prequel novel to the screen. Related Stories 'The Odyssey' Artisans on Casting Samantha Morton as Circe, Creating Her Costume and Building Her Witchy Hut Sequels, Subtitles and Spring Releases: How the Best Picture Race Is Rewriting the Academy’s Playbook One challenge Daigeler faced was meeting Close’s request that each outfit felt connected, creating a through line that explained why Drusilla changes from one look to the next. Despite the drastic differences between each outfit, Daigeler established continuity through the character’s accessories, most notably a collection of gold medals and military-inspired epaulets that created a sense of authority. “She wears all these medals, because somehow she thinks she is the top general of the capital,” Daigeler tells Variety . And, not dissimilar to red-bottomed Louboutin shoes, Daigeler gave Drusilla dramatically long black nails that were painted red underneath to show her abundant wealth. The character’s Capitol allegiance also went beyond her wardrobe, with Spencer overseeing her hair and makeup. While creating the looks, Spencer relied heavily on Collins’ source material to remain faithful to the author’s vision. title: 'Aquamarine' TV Series Greenlit at Disney+, Disney Channel
summary: Disney+ and Disney Channel greenlight Aquamarine series, creating upcoming casting opportunities for teen and family-market actors.
content: Disney has officially picked up the series adaptation of “ Aquamarine ,” Variety has learned. The live-action series will air on both Disney Channel and Disney+ . It was originally announced with a pilot order back in June. The series stars Kenzi Richardson, Briella Guiza, Theodore Dalton, and Annika Reese. Emma Roberts and Jake McDorman, who both starred in the original 2006 film, will reprise their roles in the series. Related Stories 'The Odyssey' Oscar Campaign Kicks Off With 8 New Revelations, From Tom Holland’s Shorter Skirt to Pattinson’s Rejected Wig and a Trojan Horse Stuck in Customs 'The Odyssey' Takes Imax to Biggest Quarterly Revenue to Date “‘Aquamarine’ is a timeless coming-of-age story, and we’re excited to bring its humor, heart and sense of wonder to a new generation,” said Ayo Davis, president of Disney Kids & Family. “At its core, it’s a story about the power of friendship, self-discovery and believing in yourself. And with a stellar cast led by Kenzi Richardson, there’s a magical quality to this story that I think audiences everywhere will really connect with.” The logline for the show states, “When teenager Coral (Richardson) moves to a dreamy seaside town, she begins unraveling the truth behind her mother’s disappearance — and discovers her mother is a mermaid, awakening magical powers in Coral just as secrets beneath the waves threaten to surface.” The project hails from writer and executive producer Sarah Watson (“The Bold Type”), with the film’s director, Elizabeth Allen Rosenbaum, directing the pilot and executive producing. Susan Cartsonis, who produced the film, also executive produces. Both Roberts and McDorman are executive producers on the series. John Quaintance and Jessica Bendinger wrote the original film, which was based on a novel of the same name by Alice Hoffman. Quintance, Bendinger, and Hoffman are not involved in the series. title: 'The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives: Orange County' Renewed for Season 2 at Hulu
summary: Hulu renews The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives: Orange County, extending unscripted employment and potential hosting or narration gigs.
content: Hulu is continuing the “Secret Lives” universe. “ The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives: Orange County ” has been renewed for a 20-episode second season after a quite successful first season. The debut season, which dropped on Nov. 12, drove 35 million hours globally in its first 11 days on Hulu and Disney+; the premiere landed 12% ahead of Season 5 of the flagship series. Overall, the franchise has driven over half a billion total hours globally. A spinoff of Utah-set headline-making “The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives,” this season’s cast included Ashleigh Pease, Aspyn Ovard, Jen Affleck, Bobbi Althoff, Avery Woods, Salomé Andrea, McCall DaPron, Jordan McClanahan and Madison Bontempo. DaPron’s sister, Mayci Neeley, is a cast member on the original “Secret Lives of Mormon Wives” and made a cameo on Season 1 of the spinoff; Affleck is also a cast member on both series. While some of the women — DaPron and McClanahan, in particular — are current members of the Mormon church, not everyone in the group is on the same page about religion. “Technically, I am baptized into the Mormon Church. I don’t identify with being Mormon, but I’ve been to the Mormon Church a million times. There’s so much Mormon influence in my life, even just with getting married at 19 and having kids young — the culture has shaped me so much, whether I like that or not,” Ovard told Variety ahead of the Season 1 debut. “I think there’s so much [the cast] can gain from each other. title: ‘Dancing With The Stars: The Next Pro’ Renewed For Season 2 At ABC & Prepares To Move Filming To LA
summary: ABC renews Dancing With the Stars: The Next Pro, moving to LA and expanding access for dancers and crew.
content: EXCLUSIVE : Adele Zaikman, the Israeli-Ukrainian Latin ballroom dancer and choreographer, landed a spot as a professional on the current season of Dancing with the Stars after winning spinoff The Next Pro earlier this year. Expect more dancers like Zaikman after ABC renewed Dancing with the Stars: The Next Pro for a second season. The show is also bucking the trend of big-ticket competition shows moving out of Los Angeles by moving its second season to California, having shot the first season in Australia. Deadline understands that the BBC Studios-produced show has been successful in its bid to receive the California tax credit. This would make it only the second unscripted show to receive the credit after Netflix’s upcoming series Schooled!, which comes from YouTuber Mark Rober and Jimmy Kimmel’s production company Kimmelot. It would also become the first show to successfully score the tax credit in order to relocate to California, which was one of the core missions of the California Film & Television Jobs Act. Watch on Deadline It is a massive boon for the business in California, given that the pendulum has been swinging the other way recently with shows such as American Idol moving to Georgia and The Masked Singer moving to New Jersey. The first season of The Next Pro employed around 110 local cast and crew and contributed an estimated A$7.2M ($5M) to the local Australian economy, per Screen Queensland. The law, otherwise known as California Assembly Bill 1138, was signed in to law in 2025 by Gov. Gavin Newsom, expanding the tax credits system to include unscripted shows for the first time. The act now covers “large-scale competition shows” with around 15% of its budget allocated to relocating television series. The Next Pro will return next year for its second season. title: The Extraordinary Music Worthy of an Extraordinary Life in ‘W.E.B. Du Bois: Rebel with a Cause’
summary: The documentary's team shows how integrating a subject's musical roots can deepen storytelling—insightful for scoring and directing choices.
content: Rita Coburn ‘s “ W.E.B. Du Bois: Rebel with a Cause ” is an extraordinary documentary about an extraordinary man, a film that spans nearly 100 years in two hours, yet never feels rushed or superficial. In her storytelling, Coburn shares with her subject a talent for distilling complex ideas and expressing them with force and clarity; the result is a movie that fully honors the breadth and depth of Du Bois’ achievements as a groundbreaking Black writer, historian, and activist. One of Coburn’s most potent tools in this regard is the music by composer Kathryn Bostic , who previously collaborated with the director on “Marian Anderson: The Whole World in Her Hands.” Bostic incorporates a wide array of styles and influences in her score, which references the various types of music Du Bois encountered and appreciated as a Black intellectual but isn’t beholden to them; as evocative of Bach and American folk music as it is of 19th-century spirituals and Asian motifs, it’s the sonic equivalent of Du Bois’ literary works. Related Stories ‘Coward’ Trailer: Lukas Dhont’s Belgian Oscar Entry Is a Queer Stunner 26 Years After He Wrote ‘Meet the Parents,’ John Hamburg Brings Comedy Back to Theaters with ‘Focker In-Law’ The scope of the project required Bostic to come at the material from multiple angles and perspectives. “Rita and I talked about what types of touchstones we needed to define the narrative musically,” Bostic told IndieWire. “There was the regional touchstone, the era-specific touchstone, the interior emotional aspects that we wanted to heighten with music. Then there’s always the discovery process as you begin to create.” For Bostic, that discovery process is one of the most exciting aspects of film composing. title: Frederick Wiseman's Complete Filmography to Be Distributed by Janus Films
summary: Janus Films will distribute Frederick Wiseman's complete works, expanding access for studying landmark documentary craft.
content: If you wanted to be a completionist for the movies of documentary legend Frederick Wiseman , or if you have a blind spot for Wiseman’s formalist portraits of American institutions dating back decades, today is your lucky day. Janus Films has acquired the North American distribution rights to the complete collection of 45 feature films from Wiseman’s career dating back to his seminal “Titicut Follies” in 1967, and Janus plans to distribute all of them beginning January 1, 2027. Janus already has a library that includes the works of Agnès Varda, Ingmar Bergman, Akira Kurosawa, Chantal Akerman, and Edward Yang, so Wiseman finds himself in good company. Related Stories Movie Theaters in 2026: Filmmakers and Exhibitors on What’s Good, What’s Bad, and What’s Changing Mike Plante, Sundance Film Festival Shorts Programmer, Dies at 56 Specific distribution plans haven’t been announced yet, be it whether these films are going to be seen theatrically, via streaming, or on physical release. But Wiseman’s early films, everything from “Titicut Follies” in 1967 through “State Legislature” in 2007 have been restored in 4K by Wiseman’s Zipporah Films. “La Danse” (2009) through his final feature “ Menus-Plaisirs – Les Troisgros ” (2023) will be available in their original digital formats. This is the first time any distributor other than Zipporah Films is licensing Wiseman’s work in North America, so the hope is that the late documentarian can now reach an even greater audience. It wasn’t until as recently as 2024, that Wiseman’s movies were even all available in digital formats . “We couldn’t imagine a better home in North America for Frederick Wiseman ’s films than with Janus Films,” said Karen Konicek of Zipporah Films. “It has been an honor to work alongside Fred for so many decades, producing and distributing his films. title: ‘I See Buildings Fall Like Lightning’ Tops British Independent Film Awards’ Craft Winners
summary: BIFA honored I See Buildings Fall Like Lightning, including casting win for Shaheen Baig, boosting its ensemble’s visibility.
content: Clio Barnard’s kitchen-sink drama I See Buildings Fall Light Lightning has come out on top of the British Independent Film Awards ( BIFA ) craft category winners. The White Lotus ‘ Jason Isaacs, Little White Lies’ Leila Latif and BIFA podcast host Karis Aldridge revealed the full list of craft award winners ahead of the BIFA ceremony on Dec. 6, where the British indie film business’ brightest talents will take to Camden’s Roundhouse. Barnard’s Cannes-premiering film, starring Anthony Boyle, Joe Cole, Lola Petticrew, Daryl McCormack, and Jay Lycurgo, has claimed three craft awards: best casting for Shaheen Baig, best editing for Maya Maffioli and best music supervision for Connie Farr. Written by Enda Walsh and based on the book of the same name by Kieran Goddard, the movie charts the challenging and poignant transition into adulthood for a group of 30-year-old best friends, and won the audience award at Directors’ Fortnight on the Croisette earlier this year. Grant and Claire Foy romp through their crumbling 18th-century estate, won two BIFAs — Jacquetta Levon nabbed best make-up and hair design, and Alex Bovaired claimed best costume design. Best cinematography, sponsored by Kodak and Molinare, was awarded to André Turpin for the mesmerising snow-swept vistas of Andrew Haigh’s A Long Winter , and best production design, sponsored by ATC, went to Gareth Pugh and Carson McColl for Ink , Danny Boyle’s energetic ’60s-set angle on the birth of sensationalist tabloid journalism. Black Bear Buys Thriller 'Seeker,' Starring 'Obsession's' Cooper
 Tomlinson and 'Off Campus' Actor Mika Abdalla (EXCLUSIVE)
summary: Black Bear acquired thriller Seeker, starring Cooper Tomlinson and Mika Abdalla, signaling momentum and potential hiring as production advances.
content: Black Bear has acquired “ Seeker ,” a thriller featuring “Obsession” actor Cooper Tomlinson, “Off Campus” breakout Mika Abdalla and “Happy Death Day” star Jessica Rothe. The company has North American and U.K. distribution rights to the movie, which was introduced to buyers at this year’s AFM. Directed by Adam Carter Rehmeier and written by Michael Learner, “Seeker” follows Grant (Tomlinson), whose fiancée Caroline (Abdalla) mysteriously disappeared five years earlier. Now a ride-share driver, his life is upended when he picks up a passenger who he is convinced is responsible for her absence. As the logline teases, “What starts as a tense game of cat-and-mouse spirals into something far stranger, more disturbing, and deeply unhinged — challenging everything we think we know.” Related Stories Anne Hathaway to Receive American Riviera Award at Santa Barbara International Film Festival From a Mockbuster Version of 'The Odyssey' to a 'Jiu-Jitsu Nun': How Producers Are Keeping the Low-Budget Film Market Alive Via Streaming (and Even Lower Budgets) “’Seeker’ is exactly the type of bold and propulsive storytelling we look for at Black Bear,” said Katie Anderson, Black Bear’s executive VP of acquisitions. “Michael’s script had us all on the edge of our seats, and with Adam’s singular voice and this cast’s incredible talent, we couldn’t be more excited to bring this film to theaters.” Alex Lebovici and Learner will produce for Hammerstone Studios, with Adam McKay and Todd Schulman for HyperObject Industries, and Noah Centineo and Enzo Marc of Arkhum Productions. Samuel Hall and Warren Goz will executive-produce for North Five Six, alongside Ibrahim Mohammed, Yasmyne Mohammed, Chase Vergari, Karina Manashil, David Goldman and Andria Spring. “Seeker” will begin production in January in Washington. title: ‘Hexed’ Creatives on Telling a Modern-Day Witchcraft Story, Casting Hailee Steinfeld, and Their Favorite Easter Eggs
summary: Hexed makers discuss contemporary witchcraft tone and choosing Hailee Steinfeld, offering insight into casting priorities and worldbuilding.
content: SPOILER ALERT: This story discusses mild plot points for “ Hexed ,” opening in theaters on Wednesday. Walt Disney Animation Studios’ 65th film “Hexed” tells the story of the hidden world of witches and how, throughout history, they have been misunderstood. At its heart, however, is a story of motherhood and the powerful bond between a mother and daughter. Disney animated films often kill off a parent to propel a story forward. But the creatives behind “Hexed” embraced that important relationship. Related Stories Anne Hathaway to Receive American Riviera Award at Santa Barbara International Film Festival 'The Odyssey' Leads Critics Choice Awards Below-the-Line Shortlists With 11 Mentions as 'Dune: Part Three' and 'La Bola Negra' Follow With Eight Directed by Fawn Veerasunthorn and Jason Hand, and co-directed by Josie Trinidad, the film follows Billie ( Hailee Steinfeld ), a rebellious teen who escapes into the secret world of Hexe, a realm of witches and wizards who live in harmony with nature. Veerasunthorn explained that the story idea was originally pitched by Trinidad. “She wanted to tell a story about the hidden world of witches. What if there’s a place where they can thrive on their own? The place built by witches for witches.” More importantly, Veerasunthorn notes, Trinidad wanted to tell a story of motherhood and the true heart of the story lies in the complicated, relatable relationship between Billie and her mother, Alice (Rashida Jones). In developing Billie, she was portrayed as a modern teenager who wears combat boots and has an edgy style. Producer Yvett Merino explains that Billie oozes confidence: “She doesn’t quite fit in. There’s something that feels different about her.” The key was making the film’s main protagonist relatable. “We all go through that at some point in our lives, especially in those teenage years where you’re just trying to figure out who you are,” Merino says. “She takes her mom’s car. title: ‘SNL’ Heads to France With Canal+, NBCUniversal Unveiling Cast and Manu Payet as First Host (EXCLUSIVE)
summary: Saturday Night Live launches a French edition with Canal+, revealing its cast and Manu Payet as inaugural host.
content: “ Saturday Night Live ” is getting a French makeover, with comedian and actor Manu Payet set to host the inaugural episode on Dec. 19. Titled “SNL France,” the new French adaptation will air on pay-TV channel Canal+ , which has broadcast the original American “SNL” for more than a decade. The 52-minute episode will air live in front of a studio audience, featuring a 10-member comedy ensemble, topical sketches, pre-recorded segments and live musical performances. Related Stories Sequels, Subtitles and Spring Releases: How the Best Picture Race Is Rewriting the Academy’s Playbook 'The Odyssey' Returns to Imax 70mm Theaters Again After Record-Breaking Run The French version is being produced under license from NBCUniversal Formats, a division of Universal Studio Group, and co-produced by Mediawan -owned Black Dynamite, Douze Doigts Production and Canal+. “For more than 50 years, ‘Saturday Night Live’ has been where audiences meet the next generation of comedy talent, and that’s exactly what CANAL+, Black Dynamite and Douze Doigts Productions have built for France,” said Suzanne Kendrick, VP of format sales and production at NBCUniversal Formats. “With Manu Payet launching the show alongside ten performers many viewers are about to discover for the first time, we’re excited for French audiences to see this iconic format through a French lens,” Kendrick added. The writing team is headed by comedy duo Hugo Benamozig and David Caviglioli, whose credits include the French comedy hits “Le Flambeau,” “Platane” and “Terrible Jungle.” The pair have also worked on Jonathan Cohen’s upcoming big-budget production “Astérix & Obélix: Les Douze Travaux.” They will lead a writers’ room that also includes cast member Lison Daniel, who recently co-wrote the script for “Call My Agent: The Movie.” Rising French R&B artist RnBoi, the first artist signed to Aya Nakamura’s label Nakamura Industrie, will be the inaugural musical guest and will perform a new track written for the show. title:
Oobah Butler Wants to Expose the World's Stupidest Industries, but They
 Get Worse Faster Than He Can Plan His Stunts
summary: Prank documentarian Oobah Butler says rapid scams outpace his exposés, underscoring agility needed for timely satirical projects.
content: It’s a spectacular time to be a grifter . Basic truths keep getting harder for people to agree on, marketing is more dependent on hackable algorithms than traditional gatekeepers, and it seems like everyone is willing to uncritically listen to anyone offering them a shortcut. As Oobah Butler puts it in the first episode of his new HBO series “Scams for a Better Tomorrow,” we’re living through a “gold rush of bullshit.” If that’s the case, Butler is a prospector who hits a paystreak everywhere he looks. After beginning his career as a musician, the British performance artist has devoted much of his past decade to the art of the scam. In 2017, he made headlines for creating a TripAdvisor profile for a nonexistent restaurant that briefly became the highest-rated eatery in London . His penchant for scams has only grown since then, culminating in “ Oobah: Scams for a Better Tomorrow .” The five-episode, “Nathan for You”-esque series sees him grift his way to the top of some of the slimiest industries on the planet including wellness supplements, wine, and dating apps with an approach that blurs the line between satire and how-to guides. I naturally had to ask Butler if that was his preferred term (he had no problem with it), and how he would characterize his own unorthodox line of work. “I think it sits somewhere between gonzo journalism and comedy. And I think we’re in a moment, in a culture, that’s just so rife with inauthenticity and scamming,” Butler said, explaining that just watching run-of-the-mill advertisements on a streaming service are enough to convince you that we live in an insane world. “One in three [ads] are AI now. title: Cult Classic ‘Hundreds of Beavers’ Returns to Theaters With Poster Parodying ‘The Devils’
summary: Cult comedy Hundreds of Beavers returns to 85 cities for a holiday rerelease, signaling demand for quirky theatrical fare.
content: Mike Cheslik’s slapstick film is coming back to 85 cities for its third annual Christmas re-release A few years ago, an utterly insane slapstick masterpiece called “Hundreds of Beavers” snuck upon an unsuspecting indie film world, creating a new cult classic that has remained in at least one theater in America every day since. Now, as part of what director Mike Cheslik and producer Kurt Ravenwood hopes will become an annual tradition, “Hundreds of Beavers” will be re-released in select theaters in 85 cities. And to get fans excited, the team has released beaver-themed posters parodying three of the most talked about films of the fall among cinephiles: “You Can See Everything,” “Digger,” and Ken Russell’s “The Devils,” the NC-17 drama released uncut by Warner Bros. for the first time ever this past October. “Hundreds of Beavers” stars Ryland Tews as Jean Kayak, a man brought to ruin when beavers — played by dozens of actors in beaver suits — destroy his successful applejack brewery. Left with nothing, Jean must learn to survive as a hunter and fur trapper in the cold northern wilderness … and in the process gets into a ridiculous conflict with hundreds of beavers. In addition to the film, the re-release will have a new short made by Cheslik as part of the annual tradition. Previous shorts have introduced characters like “Bing Crosbeaver” and “Conspirabeaver,” and now they will be joined by a sinister new foe. Released in 2024 with a marketing budget of just $70,000, “Hundreds of Beavers” sold out arthouses across the country with a roadshow that caught the attention of the growing Letterboxd crowd. The film was then re-released theatrically at Christmas to promote its release on Blu-Ray, which Cheslik is now turning into an annual tradition. title: ‘Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power’ Renewed for Season 4 at Amazon Prime Video
summary: Amazon renews The Rings of Power for Season 4, extending steady series work and upcoming casting opportunities.
content: “ The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power ” has been renewed for Season 4 at Amazon Prime Video. The Tolkien series, which is set thousands of years before the books in Middle-earth, is in pre-production for the new season and will begin filming in spring 2027 at Shepperton Studios in the U.K. The renewal comes on the day the final two episodes of Season 3 are airing on Amazon Prime Video. Payne, Patrick McKay, and the entire creative team. We look forward to bringing fans even deeper into the rich world of Tolkien’s Second Age.” “The Lord of the Rings: Rings of Power” stars Cynthia Addai-Robinson, Robert Aramayo, Owain Arthur, Maxim Baldry, Jamie Campbell Bower, Morfydd Clark, Ismael Cruz Córdova, Charles Edwards, Trystan Gravelle, Ciarán Hinds, Tyroe Muhafidin, Sophia Nomvete, Lloyd Owen, Andrew Richardson, Charlie Vickers, Benjamin Walker and Daniel Weyman. The third season of “The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power” was produced by showrunners and executive producers J.D. Payne and Patrick McKay, who are joined by executive producers Lindsey Weber, Kate Hazell, Justin Doble and Charlotte Brändström, who also directs. Matthew Penry-Davey is a producer and Ally O’Leary Cantrell, Tim Keene, and Andrew Lee are co-producers.

Movie Theaters in 2026: Filmmakers and Exhibitors on What's Good,
 What's Bad, and What's Changing
summary: Industry leaders outline 2026 theatrical trends: shorter windows, eventized releases, selective booking, reshaping hiring and marketing for talent.
content: In 1948, movie studios held a monopoly in entertainment, owning the means of producing and distributing films, and the theaters themselves. The 1948 Paramount Decrees (named after the studio that pioneered the vertical integration) required studios to give up one of the three options. They decided to give up exhibition. The choice was easy: With low margins on ticket sales and the need to constantly bring audiences in, who wanted to run a movie theater ? 70 years later, movie studios again faced the possibility of giving up on exhibition. The rise of streaming was said to bring about the end of theaters as we know them. But the COVID-19 pandemic brought exhibition to its closest brink of extinction yet. Related Stories Mike Plante, Sundance Film Festival Shorts Programmer, Dies at 56 Will Robert Pattinson’s Bond Casting Help Land Him His First Oscar Nomination? “COVID allowed people to acknowledge their inner recluse,” Tim League, the co-founder and former CEO of Alamo Drafthouse , told IndieWire. After the global pandemic, lockdown protocols forced movie theaters to close for months. The luxury theater chain Arclight shuttered all its locations within weeks. Locations closed at a variety of companies, including Alamo Drafthouse. Some theaters survived off of private rentals. Even as theaters slowly reopened, COVID protocols required leaving some seats empty, meaning not all tickets could be sold. “I think there was no right move,” League added. “We laid most of our people off. We spent a lot of energy trying to build up a TVOD streaming platform which didn’t entirely work for a lot of reasons… And so we went through bankruptcy, and it was rough. We just ran out of money.” “There really was no strategy,” said Greg Laemmle, owner of the California-based independent theater chain Laemmle Theatres. title: Kevin Kline Reunites With Meryl Streep in 'The Corrections' Series at Netflix
summary: Netflix orders The Corrections, reuniting Kevin Kline and Meryl Streep, creating high-profile series roles and supporting casting openings.
content: Kevin Kline will star opposite Meryl Streep in the Netflix limited series adaptation of “ The Corrections ,” Variety has learned. Based on the novel of the same name by Jonathan Franzen, the series was originally announced with Streep attached back in April . The logline describes the show as “a sharply comic portrait of a Midwestern family whose three unmoored adult siblings desperately resist their mother’s (Streep) wish for one last Christmas together – each undone by the delusional ambitions that were supposed to save them from becoming their parents.” Related Stories 'The Odyssey' Artisans on Casting Samantha Morton as Circe, Creating Her Costume and Building Her Witchy Hut Oscar Predictions: Production Design — Could Something as Innovative and Cool as 'Backrooms' Find Love? Kline will star as Alfred Lambert, who is described as “a once-powerful patriarch who is battling the afflictions of aging. A man of strict principles and old-fashioned decorum, Alfred must come to terms with his three very modern children—a daughter whose secrets he can no longer protect, an older son who has displaced him as the authority in the family, and a wayward son whose forgiveness he yearns for.” The casting marks the latest collaboration between Kline and Streep. The two most famously worked together in the hit 1982 drama “Sophie’s Choice,” which was Kline’s feature debut and for which Streep earned her second Academy Award. Kline and Streep have also appeared onscreen together in the films “A Prairie Home Companion” and “Ricki and the Flash.” Kline is primarily known for his film roles, but has been in a number of shows in recent years. He has lent his voice to the hit Fox animated series “Bob’s Burgers” since the show began, while he also recently starred in the shows “American Classic” for MGM+ and “Disclaimer” at Apple TV. title:
26 Years After He Wrote 'Meet the Parents,' John Hamburg Brings Comedy
 Back to Theaters with 'Focker In-Law'
summary: John Hamburg launches theatrical comedy Focker In-Law, signaling renewed studio appetite for big-screen comedy roles.
content: When John Hamburg worked on “ Meet the Parents ” as a writer over 25 years ago, it seemed like there were well-resourced comedies opening in theaters every week. Returning to the series this year for the third sequel, “ Focker In-Law ,” which he directed as well as wrote, the filmmaker was fully aware that big screen comedies had become a rare treat. “We felt like it had been so long since this type of comedy had been in movie theaters that we wanted to do everything we could to make it feel theatrical,” Hamburg told IndieWire. To that end, Hamburg and cinematographer Barry Peterson decided to shoot widescreen for the first time in Focker history, eschewing the 1.85:1 frame established by director Jay Roach in the first film (and perpetuated in Roach’s “Meet the Rockers” in 2004 and Paul Weitz’s “Little Fockers” in 2010) in favor of a more expansive 2.40:1 aspect ratio. It’s a pivotal decision that not only gives “Focker In-Law” a visual elegance, but showcases the ensemble performances in compositions that make the most out of the subtle interchanges and reactions between characters, often registered with the subtlety that comes from allowing the comedy to play out within the frame rather than via emphatic cuts. title: Netflix Closes $380 Million Acquisition of Radford Studio Center
summary: Netflix bought the Radford lot for $380M, expanding Los Angeles stages and likely boosting local casting and crew demand.
content: Netflix is the proud new owner of Radford Studio Center , the 98-year-old soundstage complex that was home to “Gunsmoke,” “The Mary Tyler Moore Show,” and “Seinfeld.” The streamer is set to close the $380 million acquisition this afternoon, the company said in a statement. The facility last sold to Hackman Capital Partners for $1.85 billion at the peak of the L.A. production market in 2021. The subsequent downturn in production volume and the rise in interest rates forced Hackman to default on its $1.1 billion loan, and ultimately to cede the property to its lender, Goldman Sachs. Related Stories 'The Odyssey' Returns to Imax 70mm Theaters Again After Record-Breaking Run Steven Spielberg Calls ‘The Odyssey’ a ‘Showstopper’ and ‘One of the Greatest Things’ Matt Damon Has Ever Done Netflix first emerged as a buyer of the 55-acre site in Studio City last spring. Goldman formally took the property back at a foreclosure auction on Tuesday, the final step before the deal with Netflix could close. The purchase marks a significant investment in Los Angeles for Netflix, which has made similar investments in Albuquerque, N.M., and Fort Monmouth, N.J., in recent years. “There’s still a long way to go, but we are hopeful that with the partnership of the State of California and the City of Los Angeles, this will be the start of a meaningful new investment in California’s film industry,” the company said in a statement on Tuesday. “This city is home to us. We’re excited to keep investing here and finding more ways to entertain the world, while supporting the writers, builders, electricians, drivers, designers, and talent who make L.A., California, and the entertainment industry so special.” Hackman Capital Partners proposed a $1 billion renovation of the aging Radford lot in 2023. Netflix is expected to continue that ongoing entitlement process with the city as it looks to preserve its development options and its ability to respond to market conditions. title: ‘Naughty’ vs ‘Nasty’: Universal and Warner Bros. Battle Over Titles for New Jennifer Aniston, Jenna Ortega Movies (EXCLUSIVE)
summary: Universal and Warner Bros. dispute similar titles, risking marketing delays for Jennifer Aniston and Jenna Ortega films.
content: Two similarly titled movies are causing a war of words between Universal and Warner Bros . Pictures. The legacy studios are locked in a stalemate over dueling projects that sound alike and are set to hit theaters around the same time, five sources tell Variety . The first is “ Naughty ,” Olivia Wilde’s raucous Christmas comedy starring Jennifer Aniston. The other is “ Nasty ,” Mary Bronstein’s psychological drama led by Jenna Ortega, which will roll out under Warner’s new indie label Clockwork. Universal slated “Naughty” for Nov. 5, 2027, after registering the name with the Motion Picture Association in 2023, according to two sources. Clockwork, the nascent shingle run by Neon veteran Christian Parkes, has not officially set a date for “Nasty,” though four sources say the film is also eyeing a November 2027 release. Related Stories 'The Odyssey' Takes Imax to Biggest Quarterly Revenue to Date 'The Odyssey' Leads Critics Choice Awards Below-the-Line Shortlists With 11 Mentions as 'Dune: Part Three' and 'La Bola Negra' Follow With Eight Generally, studios go to great lengths to avoid delivering movies with similar-sounding names — much less launching them in the same corridor. “Naughty” and “Nasty” aren’t alike in genre or subject matter. “Naughty,” featuring Aniston and Peter Dinklage, follows a single mom who has to convince Santa Claus to testify at her divorce hearing. “Nasty,” Bronstein’s follow-up to “If I Had Legs I’d Kick You,” revolves around an elite gymnast competing for a spot on the Olympic team while dealing with her manipulative coach. Yet insiders at Universal and Warner Bros. feel the fact that the titles are basically synonyms could confuse moviegoers. Further complicating the matter is that LuckyChap, Margot Robbie’s prolific film and TV production shop, is backing both projects. Universal and Clockwork declined to comment. The spat is headed toward a formal review by the MPA, which has a 101-year-old department called the Title Registration Bureau
